newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Tuesday led by early-maturing contracts mainly due to a rise on the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 12.50 percent from 10.49 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell slightly to 3.03 million lots from 3.2 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said the strong performance of the domestic A share markets and a new A share issue on the Shanghai stock exchange were the major factors fanning short-term fund demand on the repo market on Tuesday.

"Heavy institutional borrowing pushed up the early-maturing contracts, in particular the three-day contract," said one trader. The rate for the three-day contract surged to 19.0 percent on Tuesday from Monday's 7.5 percent.
The repo rates are likely to move at the current high level in the next few days due to a number of new A share issues and listings, traders said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down on Tuesday in very thin trading mainly because most investors have their eyes on the rising A share markets, traders said.
The most actively traded three-year bond that matures in August 2000 fell to 107.74 yuan from 107.67 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell heavily to a very thin 574,889 lots from 801,509 lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to move narrowly around the current level in the short-term.
